title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models

data.title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models
data.research_question: What information does the MLA bottleneck preserve or discard, and how does it reshape the internal circuits of a transformer?

models_and_data.quote: training a 114M-parameter MLA transformer (pretrained on a web/code/math mixture, fine-tuned on TinyStories)
The model was pretrained for 16,500 steps on a mixed corpus

60% FineWeb-Edu [Penedo et al., 2024] (general web text, for foundational language and grammar), 25% The Stack [Kocetkov et al., 2022] (source code, for coding logic and structured reasoning), and 15% OpenWebMath [Paster et al., 2023]
It was then fine-tuned for 7,200 steps on TinyStories [Eldan & Li, 2023], achieving a perplexity of 4.3 on the TinyStories validation set.
We use a BPE tokenizer with vocabulary size 32,768.
All interpretability analyses in this paper are run on the fine-tuned checkpoint, using TinyStories-distribution passages as the analysis input unless otherwise stated
All experiments are inference-only and run on a single NVIDIA T4 GPU.

protocol.quote: Decompose compression matrices WDKV and WDQ to measure effective dimensionality.
Classify all 24 × 8 = 192 heads by function (previous-token, induction, BOS-sink, local window).
Compare what linguistic features are linearly decodable from cKV (128-dim) vs. the residual stream (512-dim).
Measure how strongly corruption-induced changes to cKV at each layer correlate with degraded predictions, as a lightweight proxy for causal importance.
Add Gaussian noise (σ = 3.0) to early token embeddings (positions 1–3), and re-run the model on the corrupted input (5 noise trials per example).

For each layer, compute the cosine dissimilarity between clean and corrupted cKV at every position, then scale the resulting per-(layer, position) disruption map by the trial’s drop in probability on the correct next token, max(0, pclean − pcorrupt ).

key_results.claim: cKV learns a content-only representation preserving entity identity while discarding position.
key_results.quote: the cKV bottleneck learns a pure content representation, preserving entity identity (98% retention) while discarding positional information (near chance accuracy)

key_results.claim: All detected induction heads co-locate at Layer 12.
key_results.quote: All five detected induction heads are at Layer 12 exclusively.

key_results.claim: Layer 15 has both highest disruption-attribution score and highest SVD effective rank.
key_results.quote: Layer 15 has the highest disruption-attribution score (1.0 normalized) and the highest SVD effective rank (88/128).

key_results.claim: The KV bottleneck is globally over-provisioned.
key_results.quote: On average, the model uses only 46% of its 128-dim KV bottleneck capacity.

key_results.claim: Mean effective rank of WDKV is below full capacity.
Fine-tuned model reaches low TinyStories validation perplexity.
key_results.quote: achieving a perplexity of 4.3 on the TinyStories validation set.

key_results.claim: Position probe accuracy from cKV is near chance.
key_results.quote: c_KV accuracy (21.7%) is barely above chance (6.25%)

limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Every finding in this paper (induction-head co-location at Layer 12, the Layer 15 semantic hub, the specific retention percentages) comes from one training run of one 114M-parameter model.
Our claim that induction heads co-locate “unlike” standard MHA rests on a qualitative comparison to Olsson et al. [2022], who studied different models, different scale, and different training data.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Narrow analysis domain after TinyStories fine-tuning.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: all of our interpretability analyses (probing, attention-head taxonomy, disruption attribution) are run on the model after fine-tuning on TinyStories, using TinyStories-distribution passages as input.
Our probing results establish what is linearly decodable from cKV ; they cannot rule out nonlinearly encoded information the model could still exploit downstream.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Disruption attribution is correlational, not causal patching.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our signal is correlational: it identifies layers whose cKV changes coincide with degraded predictions, not layers where restoring information is proven to fix predictions.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Model scale is far below production MLA models.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: At 114M parameters, our model is roughly 2,000× smaller than DeepSeek-V2 (236B) and over 5,800× smaller than DeepSeek-V3 (671B)

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The paper studies a 114M MLA model, not Gemma 4 E2B; its findings about KV-shared layers 15-34 and per-layer embeddings are not directly tested.
The disruption-attribution method uses a single trial-level probability-drop scalar, so layer importance may be confounded by examples where corruption does not reduce the target probability.
Head taxonomy thresholds and classification criteria are not fully specified, so induction-head co-location may be sensitive to detection thresholds and the small 50-passage, length-64 analysis set.
Probing only on TinyStories-distribution text after fine-tuning may inflate entity/position separability and may not transfer to broader pretraining or Gemma activation distributions.
The over-provisioning claim is based on SVD effective rank at a 99% energy threshold and is not validated by actual rank ablation or heterogeneous-rank training.
The study lacks activation patching, logit lens, and factual-recall tracing, so it cannot directly support causal circuit claims comparable to the lab's planned Gemma internals work.
data.relevance_to_lab: Relevant as a mechanistic-interpretability template for KV-compression and induction-head analysis, but it studies a 114M MLA model rather than Gemma 4 E2B; its SVD, probing, and disruption-attribution methods could inform KV-shared layer analysis, while its lack of activation patching, logit lens, factual-recall tracing, and different architecture limit direct transfer.

protocol.step: Perform SVD analysis of the KV and query compression matrices at every layer to estimate effective dimensionality.
protocol.quote: SVD Analysis (Section 4.1): Decompose compression matrices WDKV and WDQ to measure effective dimensionality.

protocol.step: Classify all 24 × 8 = 192 attention heads by previous-token, induction, BOS-sink, and local-window function.
protocol.quote: Classify all 24 × 8 = 192 heads by function (previous-token, induction, BOS-sink, local window).

protocol.step: Train linear probes using 12,800 token positions from 100 passages of 128 tokens with an 80/20 train-validation split.
protocol.quote: Probes are trained on 12,800 token positions (100 passages × 128 tokens) with a 80/20 train/val split.

protocol.step: Run the model on clean input while caching all cKV activations.
protocol.quote: Run the model cleanly, caching all cKV activations.

protocol.step: Corrupt positions 1–3 with Gaussian noise of σ = 3.0 and rerun the model using five noise trials per example.
protocol.quote: Add Gaussian noise (σ = 3.0) to early token embeddings (positions 1–3), and re-run the model on the corrupted input (5 noise trials per example).

protocol.step: Compute per-layer, per-position clean-versus-corrupted cKV cosine dissimilarity and scale it by the trial-level probability drop.
protocol.quote: For each layer, compute the cosine dissimilarity between clean and corrupted cKV at every position, then scale the resulting per-(layer, position) disruption map by the trial’s drop in probability on the correct next token, max(0, pclean − pcorrupt ).

protocol.step: Do not restore clean activations during the corrupted forward pass; treat the resulting attribution as correlational.
protocol.quote: Unlike classic activation patching, we do not restore clean activations into the corrupted forward pass and re-measure the output;

key_results.claim: The cKV bottleneck behaves as a content-only representation, preserving entity identity while discarding positional information.
key_results.quote: the cKV bottleneck learns a pure content representation, preserving entity identity (98% retention) while discarding positional information (near chance accuracy), validating MLA’s architectural separation of content from position via RoPE;

key_results.claim: All detected induction heads are localized exclusively to Layer 12.
key_results.quote: All five detected induction heads are at Layer 12 exclusively.

key_results.claim: Layer 15 is the semantic hub, jointly showing the highest effective rank and disruption-attribution score.
key_results.quote: Layer 15 has the highest disruption-attribution score (1.0 normalized) and the highest SVD effective rank (88/128).

key_results.claim: The KV bottleneck is globally over-provisioned and exhibits substantial heterogeneity.
key_results.quote: Key finding: On average, the model uses only 46% of its 128-dim KV bottleneck capacity. At the 90% energy threshold, only 17 dimensions suffice on average—suggesting significant over-provisioning.

key_results.claim: The highest group-level attribution occurs in the semantic-integration layer group.
key_results.quote: 3. Semantic integration (L13–19, attribution score 0.88): The “high-attribution cluster” where corruption to cKV is most strongly associated with degraded predictions.

key_results.claim: Despite hosting all induction heads, Layer 12 has only moderate disruption attribution.
key_results.quote: Layer 12 paradox: Despite containing all induction heads, Layer 12 has only a moderate disruptionattribution score (0.50).

key_results.claim: Caching only the shared cKV produces substantial KV-cache savings relative to standard MHA.
key_results.quote: MLA achieves dramatic reductions in KV-cache memory, up to 81% compared to standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA), without sacrificing generation quality.

key_results.claim: The authors estimate that heterogeneous layer-specific bottleneck allocation could yield further cache savings.
key_results.quote: In our model, this would reduce KV-cache memory by an additional ∼30% with minimal performance impact.

limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Every finding in this paper (induction-head co-location at Layer 12, the Layer 15 semantic hub, the specific retention percentages) comes from one training run of one 114Mparameter model.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The comparison with standard MHA is qualitative rather than a matched, controlled baseline.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our claim that induction heads co-locate “unlike” standard MHA rests on a qualitative comparison to Olsson et al. [2022], who studied different models, different scale, and different training data.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: All interpretability analyses use a fine-tuned model and TinyStories-distribution input, limiting domain generality.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: However, all of our interpretability analyses (probing, attention-head taxonomy, disruption attribution) are run on the model after fine-tuning on TinyStories, using TinyStories-distribution passages as input.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Linear probing cannot exclude nonlinearly encoded information.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our probing results establish what is linearly decodable from cKV ; they cannot rule out nonlinearly encoded information the model could still exploit downstream.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Disruption attribution is correlational and does not demonstrate that restoring a layer fixes predictions.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Our signal is correlational: it identifies layers whose cKV changes coincide with degraded predictions, not layers where restoring information is proven to fix predictions.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The 114M-parameter model is far smaller than the production models that motivate the work.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: At 114M parameters, our model is roughly 2,000× smaller than DeepSeek-V2 (236B) and over 5,800× smaller than DeepSeek-V3 (671B), the production models that motivate this study.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The work is framed as hypothesis-generating rather than a definitive characterization of MLA.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Given these limitations, we present this work as an initial, hypothesis-generating investigation into MLA’s internals rather than a definitive characterization.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The study lacks direct evidence that induction heads consume entity features rather than other content encoded in cKV.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We do not have direct evidence that the induction heads specifically consume entity features rather than other content encoded in cKV ; this would require a more targeted causal experiment

threats_not_stated_by_authors: No confidence intervals, repeated-probe seeds, or statistical tests are reported for layerwise probe accuracies, retention values, head scores, or layer rankings, so small differences may reflect noise.

Probe optimization details such as regularization, initialization, class weighting, stopping criteria, and random seeds are not specified in the provided text, limiting reproducibility and potentially affecting near-ceiling versus near-chance comparisons.
Head-classification thresholds and sensitivity to the 50-passage sample are not reported, so exclusive Layer-12 induction localization could depend on metric cutoffs or passage sampling.
SVD effective rank is measured on projection weights without data-dependent activation covariance or a functional bottleneck ablation, so it may not equal effective information capacity.
The Gaussian corruption protocol has no reported noise-scale robustness sweep and may induce off-manifold effects that do not generalize to natural model errors.
The proposed heterogeneous rank allocation is not implemented or benchmarked, so its estimated cache saving and minimal performance impact remain speculative.
data.relevance_to_lab: Moderate methodological relevance but no direct architectural replication. The paper provides layerwise linear probes, head-function scoring, induction-head localization, and corruption-based attribution templates that can be redirected to Gemma 4 E2B's KV-shared layers 15–34 and per-layer embeddings. Its strongest lab-relevant warning is that corruption without clean-activation restoration is correlational; Gemma studies using activation patching can test causality directly. The paper does not study Gemma, per-layer embeddings, logit lens, factual recall, multilingual inputs, long-context behavior, or CPU execution, and its 24-layer MLA/cKV architecture and TinyStories setting differ, so layer indices and findings should not be assumed to transfer.
